answer: An agent market for pearl and marble uses a capacity-limited endorsement graph as its admission bridge. Validators allocate trust from fixed honest roots to all accounts jointly. Each edge's capacity is shared across recipients. One unit admits one agent. Adding clone-to-clone edges cannot enlarge the cluster's incoming cut, so each extra admitted alias consumes another scarce unit of external endorsement. Contradictory signed attestations revoke a voucher's capacity. Parallel keys cannot reuse allocated capacity. This assumes trustworthy roots. Buying or corrupting endorsers remains possible.
